title: Sales By Representative filter, column and dash cells look as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Today has one invoiced split work order (Labor {Sales-rep-A}, Parts {Sales-rep-B}) and one invoiced part sale with no shop supplies.
  • The design canvas is open in another tab at page 4, boards 4.4 to 4.10.
    For example: the canvas is https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open for today in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide at 100% zoom.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Compare the default report with boards 4.4 and 4.5.
  2. Open the Sales Type filter; compare with board 4.6.
  3. Open the column selector, turn Sales Type on and expand both representatives; compare with boards 4.8 to 4.10.
  4. Read the Shop Supplies cell on {Sales-rep-B}'s Parts row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one row per representative; no Sales Type column by default.
  • Step 2: the filter lists "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales", all ticked.
  • Step 3: "Sales Type" is first in the column selector; the column shows after Status with "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales"; columns line up as in the pictures and nothing overlaps.
  • Step 4: a dash, not $0.00.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10890; story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative); story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type); PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 8 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R15, S5-R19, S5-R20, S5-R21, S8-R1, read 19 Oct 2026. Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, page 4, boards 4.4 to 4.10, used for the picture to compare against. Source-verified 19 October 2026. The build is not yet available to check this case against.

The design shows $0.00 under Shop Supplies on the Parts row (boards 4.5 and 4.10). The PRD says a dash; this case follows the PRD, and the difference is on the product owner's question list. Whether a part sale with no shop supplies shows a dash or $0.00 is also on the list.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero.”
  • S5-R19: “An invoice row carries a "Sales Type" column, after Status, reading "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" or "Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R20: “The Sales Type column is offered in the report's column selector, first in its list.”
  • S5-R21: “The Sales Type column is off by default on screen, for every user.”
  • S8-R1: “Sales By Representative has a "Sales Type" filter with three options, in this order: "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales". All three are selected by default.”
